correctness.rationale: All normalized maximizers are strict-convex vertices of a compact anchored Lipschitz polytope. Connected tight edges force integral values, and diameter two restricts to 0,1,2. The extremes correspond to two cross-disjoint edge families of K_n with disjoint endpoint supports. For capacities A=C(n-t,2), B=C(t,2), the exact continuous envelope Q<=N min(2A-v,2B+v)-v^2 is maximized at full capacities whenever D=A-B<=N/2. Its full-capacity objective increases strictly with t(n-t). When D>N/2, t<n/4 and Q<N^2/4+N*n*(n-4)/16, strictly below the balanced value by the explicit even/odd positive gaps in RESULT.md. Binary potentials are strictly smaller. Equality forces the complete two-block levels and yields the exact multiplicity; computations are corroborative, not proof.

originality.rationale: General graph spread and integer-valued optimizing potentials were established in Alon–Boppana–Spencer 1998 (author-hosted complete paper, Theorem 2.1). Addario-Berry–Janson–McDiarmid 2009/2012 study random graph families and known complete-graph/product facts; Yancey 2017 studies variance-optimal graph functions, particularly trees, cycles and product concentration. None of the inspected material gives the triangular graph J(n,2) exact variance norm, complete balanced-two-block classification, or multiplicity. Kneser pair graphs have complementary adjacency and their metric optimization does not imply this result. External and indexed searches are limited, hence qualified PASS.
residual_risks: Unindexed or differently named literature may already compute the same exact J(n,2) norm and equality family.
Keyword searches and selective full-text inspection cannot establish universal bibliographic priority.
The related Kneser pair result is a complementary-graph comparison and must not be mistaken for novelty proof.

value.rationale: Determines a natural exact Lipschitz-to-centered-L2 embedding norm on the complete infinite triangular/Johnson two-subset graph family, with every maximizer and its exponentially growing multiplicity. The balanced disjoint-support optimization supplies structural information not implied by integrality or a generic variance bound. Fixed rank-two Johnson graphs are a canonical distance-regular family, and both the exact formula and equality geometry are motivated invariants rather than arbitrary finite slices.
